probe.format_note: 16:9 landscape, single full-frame film (720 frames at 24 fps). Stereo AAC 48 kHz, continuous track with no silence longer than 0.3 s at -40 dB (mean -16.8 dB, peak -1.8 dB); its content (music, voice, effects) was not analysed and is never reused. Container title is English third-party copy (ignored).

mode.alt_film_mode: REEL when the content package is a hook-problem-solution-CTA reel with no recurring character
mode.why: third-party film of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and look only, never its shots one by one, its characters, its documents, its map or its copy (owner note); the reference is a character story that dives into an explanatory document and comes back to the characters, which is the EXPLAINER grammar

buildable_note: 5.75-24.5 s (18.75 of 30 s) is flat vector infographic on paper and is code-native; 0-5.75 s and 24.5-30 s (11.25 s, about 38%) are painted cartoon illustration with character acting, which code cannot match: those scenes need illustrated stills (generated or supplied) animated in code (push-ins, parallax, small cut-outs), or must be rebuilt as flat vector characters. Warning per D55: painted illustration.

ignored.why: all characters (the girl in the mustard hoodie, the moustached desk agent, the grey tabby cat in glasses) and the airport check-in setting are third-party characters and scenery; never reused, never redrawn as look-alikes. Our characters and setting come from the voiceover.

all document content and English copy ('PET PASSPORT', 'EUROPEAN UNION', 'EU PET PASSPORT', 'Description of animal', 'Marking of animal', the pet name, microchip number, dates, batch code, 'Dr A. Moreau', 'VALID', 'MATCH', 'Within the EU', 'Outside the EU', 'Rules vary', the three question chips, 'CHECK BEFORE YOU TRAVEL', the footnote) is third-party copy and figures; never reused as text or numbers
the circle-of-stars emblem is an official institutional symbol; never reused or imitated
the map of Europe and its routes are the reference's subject; a map appears in our film only if the voiceover needs one, drawn from our own content

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 at 480 px (5 sheets, all viewed; frame time = (sheet-1)*6 + index*0.5 s); scene detect gt(scene,0.3): cuts at 1.08, 2.92, 4.29, 24.50, 25.58, 26.17, 28.21, 29.00 s, plus flags at 12.42 s (polaroid arrival, not a cut) and 20.25-20.42 s (gatefold reveal of the map, not a hard cut); dense sheets fps=8 at 320 px over 5-7, 14.5-16.5, 19.5-21.5 and 23.5-25.5 s (4 sheets, all viewed; frame time = start + index*0.125 s); silencedetect and volumedetect on the audio. Spans inside the document section read from the 0.5 s sheets are accurate to about ±0.25 s, those around the dense windows to about ±0.1 s. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

visual_language: A small character story that dives into the object at its centre, explains it on paper, and comes back to the characters. Medium: two registers. The story world (0-5.75 s and 24.5-30 s) is painted 2D cartoon illustration with ink outlines, soft painted shading, warm window light, paper grain and strong background blur, animated pose-to-pose with small acting beats (expressions, gestures) and slow push-ins. The explainer (5.75-24.5 s) is flat vector infographic on aged cream paper inside a dark teal frame: one opened booklet as the stage, filled step by step — header bars wipe in, typewriter values type, icons pop with overshoot, stickers fly in and land, a pen signs, a stamp presses, a magnifier checks, a bar fills, a pin drops, a stamp word slams; then a gatefold opens onto a paper map where dashed routes draw, chips stack and a ribbon banner closes the argument. Typography: heavy condensed sans caps for page titles and banners, tiny label caps over typewriter-style values, a handwritten signature and caption. Rhythm: the story shots are short (0.6-2 s, average about 1.3 s, hard cuts that follow gestures or cut in on the action); the explainer is one continuous 18.75 s sequence without a hard cut, its beats spaced about 0.3-0.6 s apart, chapters separated by a page turn and a gatefold. Arrivals are snappy with back-out overshoot (0.15-0.3 s), lines and routes draw smoothly (0.2-0.4 s), typing is linear. Palette: cream paper, dark teal surround, navy, teal, mustard, with traffic-light semantics — green for confirmed, yellow for highlighted, orange for 'it depends', red for warnings and pins. Signature moments: the object lifting out of the painted scene as a flat diagram of itself, the annotated silhouette checked by a tool, sticker-signature-stamp, the magnifier and the filling validity bar, the gatefold onto the map.
look: Flat 2D throughout, no real 3D. Story world: painted cartoon illustration, ink outlines, soft painted shading and warm interior light, visible paper grain, strong depth-of-field blur on backgrounds, no hard cast shadows. Explainer: flat vector shapes on a textured aged cream paper with slight vignetting, thin dark outlines on icons and map coasts, soft short drop shadows under stickers, photo frames, cards and the tool (paper-cutout feel), the booklet sits on a flat dark teal backdrop with a soft shadow; the only perspective moments are the page curl/turn and the gatefold fold-out; during the lift-out the painted scene is gaussian-blurred and dimmed behind the flat graphic.
code_translation: Explainer section code-native in HTML/CSS/SVG in headless Chromium: a paper texture layer (noise + vignette) under SVG content; header bars as scaleX wipes from the reading start edge; typed values by revealing whole Persian words (never splitting joined letters) with the shaped brand font; leader lines and dashed connectors as stroke-dashoffset draws; pops as scale with back-out easing; sticker fly-in as translate+rotate with a settle; signature as an SVG stroke reveal following a pen sprite; stamp as a drop with a 0.1 s squash leaving an ink mark; magnifier as a moving circular mask with a scaled copy under it; validity bar as a scaleX fill; page curl and gatefold as CSS 3D rotateY on page halves with a moving shadow gradient. Story section: painted illustration cannot be drawn in code at this quality — use illustrated stills (generated or supplied) in the same painted cartoon style, animated in code with slow push-ins, slight parallax between a blurred background layer and the characters, and pose changes by cutting between stills on beats; the lift-out transition is a blurred, dimmed copy of the last still with the flat vector card scaling out of it.
continuity: Lift-out: the object the story is about is lifted out of the scene as a flat diagram of itself, the world blurs and dims behind it, and the diagram opens to become the stage of the explanation.
One stage, many states: the whole explanation happens on one surface (a document spread) that is written, annotated, stamped and turned, instead of cutting between shots.
Chapter breaks are physical: a page corner curls and the page turns; a gatefold opens to reveal a wider view underneath.
Annotate the subject: a silhouette of the subject gets leader lines to labelled fields, so facts are attached to the body they describe.
Evidence is tied together by dashed connectors drawn between the pieces after they all appear.
Tactile verification: a tool touches the subject and a check badge pops; a magnifier passes over values and leaves highlights; a stamp gives the verdict.
A range shown as a filling bar with the case dropped onto it as a pin, so 'inside the limits' is seen, not read.
Zoom from the single case to the whole picture (one document → a map of where it applies), with a simple path and an uncertain path in different semantic colours.
The object comes back: after the explainer, the same object reappears physically in the painted scene, so the viewer knows the explanation happened inside it.
Story bookend: the film opens on a rushed action and closes on the character's relief, with a short comic insert of the second character between anxious and relieved beats.
Cuts in the story world follow a gesture or cut in on an action (a point leads to what is pointed at; a close-up of a hand on the object).
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its characters (girl, desk agent, tabby cat), the airport setting, the passport design, the circle-of-stars emblem, the map of Europe, any English copy, names, numbers or dates, or the shot order one by one.

About 38% of the reference (0-5.75 s and 24.5-30 s) is painted cartoon illustration with character acting: not buildable in code at this quality. Those scenes need illustrated stills in the same style (generated or supplied) animated in code, or a flat vector character fallback; warning per D55 (painted illustration).

Source is 16:9 landscape and the explainer stage is a two-page spread: a 9:16 film must rebuild it vertically (a single tall page, or the spread rotated with the second page below the first), keeping everything inside the 9:16 safe zone.

Explainer labels and typed values are tiny in the reference: Persian text sizes and hold times win over the reference's density (readability ranks above the reference); fewer fields per page, larger type, longer holds.

The reference reads left to right (header bars wipe from the left, page turns right to left, routes and the timeline fill left to right, the gatefold is symmetric): for Persian follow references/rtl-grammar.md — bars wipe from the right, the page turns left to right, a time bar fills right to left; typing reveals whole joined words, never letter by letter in a way that breaks joining; the signature reveal must follow Persian stroke direction.

Reference colours (cream paper, dark teal surround, navy, teal, mustard, green/yellow/orange/red semantics) map onto brand colour roles (light surface, dark background, primary, accent, success, warning, danger); never used as literal hex values. Colours were read by eye, not sampled.

The reference has a continuous audio track; our film's cuts follow the voiceover first, and L6 places accents (typing ticks, pops, stamp thud, page turn) on our own cuts rather than reusing their audio.
